methods.label: Group powers with the same base
methods.explanation:
Since \(x>y>0\), both bases are positive, so the power rules apply even when the exponents are arbitrary real numbers. Every power in the denominator is also nonzero. Grouping equal bases gives
\[
\frac{x^y y^x}{y^y x^x}
=\frac{x^y}{x^x}\frac{y^x}{y^y}
=x^{y-x}y^{x-y}.
\]
The exponents \(x-y\) and \(y-x\) are opposites. Using \(a^{-t}=1/a^t\) for \(a>0\), we obtain
\[
x^{y-x}y^{x-y}
=\frac{x^{y-x}}{y^{y-x}}.
\]
For positive bases, equal real exponents can be combined by \(a^t/b^t=(a/b)^t\). Therefore the answer is
\[
\boxed{\left(\frac{x}{y}\right)^{y-x}},
\]
choice D.
methods.levelReason: Standard precalculus power rules for positive bases give the result directly, while retaining the unrestricted real-exponent domain.
